To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the recognition of famous faces involves spatio-temporily complex neural processes that exhibit differential pattern activity changes depending upon the recognition state.
recognition of familiar face is a complex spatio-temporaly dynamic process.

the N170 and N250 face-sensitive ERP components exhibit an abrupt change at the point of overt recognition of familiar face, but that later ERP components (e.g., N400 and Late positive component) exhibit an incremental increase in activity as the moment of recognition approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the neural events occurring before and up to overt and covert recognition of famous faces.
the characterization of the neural events occurring prior to and at the time of recognition of familiar faces.
characterizing the spatio-temporal dynamics of the neural events occurring prior to and during overt recognition of famous and unfamiliar faces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
recognition of familiar and unfamiliar faces is a dynamic, complex, and spatio-temporality distributed neural process.
recognition of familiar face is a nonlinear process that is not mandatory and that it is not completely unconscious.

the recognition process of familiar faces is not a simple all-or-none process but it is rather a complex and dynamic spatio-temporal neural activity that is characterized by different ERP patterns as recognition state changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain processes involved in familiar face recognition are not all-or-none, as suggested by the abrupt change in the N170 and N250, but are instead gradual and continuous as indicated by the N400 and the late positive component
the recognition of familiar faces is characterized by an all-or-none and a gradual process.
familiar face recognition involves both gradual and all-or none processes, and that the gradual process is more prominent in the later ERP components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural processes involved during overt recognition are not necessarily the same processes involved during the covert recognition.
the brain activity related to overt recognition of famous people is not only characterized by a sudden activity increase but also by an incremental increase in the activity of later ERP responses.

the neural dynamics of overt and covert recognition of familiar faces are not the same, and that overt recognition of familiar face is a complex process involving gradual and all-or-nothing processes.
